key_insight: The paper tightens deep learning generalization bounds by making the robustness term local to sub-regions of the input space and scaling it by stable versus unstable samples.
engineering_relevance: This can give practitioners more realistic, non-vacuous error estimates for safety-critical models when choosing and validating robust neural networks.
method: Partition the input space into sub-regions.
Measure local robustness using counts of stable and unstable samples.
Combine the localized robustness term with data- and model-dependent factors to form an upper bound on generalization error.
evidence_signal: On ImageNet-trained models, the proposed bounds stayed consistently non-vacuous and were the tightest among compared methods, closely tracking empirical error across robust deep networks.
watch_item: The bound’s usefulness may still depend on how sub-regions are defined and how stable/unstable samples are estimated in practice.
paper_title: Upper Bounds on the Generalization Error of Deep Learning Models via Local Robustness and Stability
